quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Drop the jaw and round the lips slightly: 'hot' feels back and open.
quests.explanation: The tongue pulls back and the lips round slightly, giving a back, open vowel. The central vowel of 'hut' would be too forward.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is back and open with slightly rounded lips; /ʌ/ is central and unrounded with neutral lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Lips stay flat and the tongue stays in the middle. 'Run' is a lazy, quick vowel.
quests.explanation: Central and unrounded. Rounding the lips would drag it towards the vowel of 'hot'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Round the lips a little and drop the jaw for /ɒ/. Keep them flat and relaxed for /ʌ/, with the tongue further forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: After the /kl/ cluster the vowel is open and slightly rounded, like the one in 'cloth'.
quests.explanation: The lips make a slight oval at the vowel, and the /kl/ cluster before it does not remove that rounding.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Lip rounding is the clearest cue: /ɒ/ has it, /ʌ/ does not.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Round the lips a touch and open the jaw. 'Dog' sounds darker than 'dug'.
quests.explanation: Back and slightly rounded. Swap in the central vowel and you get 'dug'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short and fairly open, so duration gives no help. Listen for the darker, back quality of /ɒ/ against the brighter, more central /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Neutral lips, tongue in the middle. It should sound like a brief grunt.
quests.explanation: Keep the lips flat. Round them and you will say 'bog'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Think of the lips first: a small rounded gap for /ɒ/, a loose unrounded one for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A voiceless /ks/ ends the word, keeping the vowel short and rounded.
quests.explanation: The /ks/ follows quickly, so the rounded vowel is brief.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ sits further back and a little lower; /ʌ/ is more central. The tongue moves forward and slightly up from /ɒ/ to /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The o spelling is misleading. 'Son' sounds identical to 'sun'.
quests.explanation: A homophone of 'sun'. An o before n, m or v often hides this central vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling o can give either: 'son' has /ʌ/ and 'sock' has /ɒ/. After w, a gives /ɒ/ (want) while o often gives /ʌ/ (wonder).

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Same letter o, but this time the lips round and the jaw opens.
quests.explanation: Same letter o as in 'son' but a completely different vowel. Only the ear can sort them.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a mirror /ɒ/ shows a round opening and /ʌ/ a relaxed one, with the jaw at about the same height.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Hear it as 'bruth-'. The o in the spelling doesn't mean rounded lips.
quests.explanation: Like 'mother' and 'other', the stressed o is central and unrounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so don't wait for a length difference. Wait for darkness (rounding) versus neutrality.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: After /w/, the letter a can sound like 'o'. Round the lips and open the jaw.
quests.explanation: After /w/ the vowel pulls back and rounds, as in 'want', 'watch' and 'what'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If /ʌ/ keeps coming out as /ɒ/, relax the lips completely and let the tongue rest in the middle.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The o after w is the opposite trap. Here it is central and relaxed.
quests.explanation: 'Won', 'wonder' and 'worry' take the central vowel, while 'want' and 'watch' take the rounded one.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is back and open with slightly rounded lips; /ʌ/ is central and unrounded with neutral lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Think of the word 'what': back and rounded.
quests.explanation: Another a after /w/ that sounds like o. The /tʃ/ stays short and sharp.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Round the lips a little and drop the jaw for /ɒ/. Keep them flat and relaxed for /ʌ/, with the tongue further forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Ou plus gh looks complex, but the vowel is short and central and the ending is just /f/.
quests.explanation: Ough spells /ʌf/ here, as in 'rough' and 'enough'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Lip rounding is the clearest cue: /ɒ/ has it, /ʌ/ does not.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Round the lips lightly on the first vowel. It isn't 'cuffy'.
quests.explanation: The lips round slightly in the stressed syllable. The final -ee is only a light /i/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short and fairly open, so duration gives no help. Listen for the darker, back quality of /ɒ/ against the brighter, more central /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Back to the front-versus-central pair: this one stretches the mouth wide.
quests.explanation: The tch is just /tʃ/. The vowel is low and front with a wide jaw.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Mouth shape separates them: /æ/ stretches sideways, while /ʌ/ stays neutral and unrounded, like a short relaxed grunt.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Round the lips lightly and keep the vowel quick. The ending is only a murmur.
quests.explanation: The rounded vowel is in the stressed first syllable. The final -or is a weak schwa.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Think of the lips first: a small rounded gap for /ɒ/, a loose unrounded one for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: It isn't 'no-thing'. The first syllable is short and central.
quests.explanation: O plus th suggests a diphthong, but 'nothing', 'another' and 'other' all use the central vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ sits further back and a little lower; /ʌ/ is more central. The tongue moves forward and slightly up from /ɒ/ to /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The lips round slightly on the first vowel and the rest of the word shrinks.
quests.explanation: The rounded vowel sits in the first syllable, and the later syllables are weak and quick.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling o can give either: 'son' has /ʌ/ and 'sock' has /ɒ/. After w, a gives /ɒ/ (want) while o often gives /ʌ/ (wonder).

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The first syllable sounds like 'cull'. No lip rounding.
quests.explanation: 'Come', 'colour' and 'comfort' all share the central vowel, spelled with o.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a mirror /ɒ/ shows a round opening and /ʌ/ a relaxed one, with the jaw at about the same height.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Two syllables, the first strong. Open and rounded.
quests.explanation: The lips round in the stressed first syllable, and then a quick weak syllable follows.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so don't wait for a length difference. Wait for darkness (rounding) versus neutrality.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Compare 'lack' and 'luck'. One stretches the mouth, the other stays neutral.
quests.explanation: Central and relaxed. 'Lack' would need a much wider, more forward vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: These two sit close on the chart: /æ/ is lower and further forward. Keep the tongue tip behind the lower teeth for /æ/ only.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ou in 'cousin' sounds like the u in 'cut', not like 'cow'.
quests.explanation: Ou here sounds like the u in 'cut'. The unstressed -in reduces to a syllabic /n/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If /ʌ/ keeps coming out as /ɒ/, relax the lips completely and let the tongue rest in the middle.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: After /w/ the a is rounded and open again.
quests.explanation: The same /w/ plus a pattern as in 'want' and 'watch', and dependable in RP.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is back and open with slightly rounded lips; /ʌ/ is central and unrounded with neutral lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A rounded, open vowel after /pr/. The second syllable almost disappears.
quests.explanation: The second syllable is weak, so the first vowel is the only strong one.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Round the lips a little and drop the jaw for /ɒ/. Keep them flat and relaxed for /ʌ/, with the tongue further forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The first syllable sounds like 'mun-'. The second syllable has a different vowel.
quests.explanation: The first syllable is central. The second contains a diphthong that is not part of this contrast.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Lip rounding is the clearest cue: /ɒ/ has it, /ʌ/ does not.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The h is silent, so the word starts on a vowel sound. It is rounded and open.
quests.explanation: The h is silent, so the word begins directly on the rounded vowel, just as 'hour' begins on a vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short and fairly open, so duration gives no help. Listen for the darker, back quality of /ɒ/ against the brighter, more central /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short, loose oo. 'Cookie' is quick and relaxed, with only slight lip rounding.
quests.explanation: Short and loose, like 'book' and 'good'. Tense, protruded lips would give 'kooky'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Before dark /l/ the contrast gets muddy ('pull' versus 'pool'), so use lip protrusion and length together.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The lips round and the jaw opens on the first vowel only.
quests.explanation: Stress and rounding fall on the first syllable. The later syllables are weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Think of the lips first: a small rounded gap for /ɒ/, a loose unrounded one for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A strong first syllable, ignoring the h. A central, relaxed vowel.
quests.explanation: U is the typical spelling for this vowel, and the second syllable is a weak schwa.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ sits further back and a little lower; /ʌ/ is more central. The tongue moves forward and slightly up from /ɒ/ to /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Back to the half-open vowel. The word starts with /dʒ/ and a short vowel.
quests.explanation: The ge spells /dʒe/ and the final -tle is a syllabic /l/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If a word with /æ/ is coming out as /e/, check that the front of the tongue is low, not hovering at mid-height.
